task.description: WF-03 Step 1: reproduce ISS-0782 directly against a real running backend (real HTTP, real admin token -- not a restatement of the bug report's prose), trace to root cause, identify every affected call site in web/src/api/identity.ts that is actually exercised by the Users admin screen (UsersPage.tsx + UserDetailPage.tsx), and explain why existing tests didn't catch it. Do NOT implement the fix -- produce a diagnosis for CODE-DESIGNER.
acceptance_criteria: reproduction quotes real HTTP status codes from a live backend + real admin token, not restated bug-report prose
root cause traced to the exact router mount and the exact wrong call sites in identity.ts
confirms the real, router-backed replacement path for both users and roles listing

scoped to what the Users admin screen (UsersPage.tsx + UserDetailPage.tsx) actually calls -- explicitly separates in-scope call sites from call sites belonging to other admin screens (Groups/Tokens) or already covered by ISS-0765
explains why existing tests (mocked unit tests only) didn't catch this

result.summary:
ROOT CAUSE: lib/letflow/plugs/api_pipeline.ex line 141 mounts `Letflow.Routers.Identity` ONLY at `/identity` (`forward("/identity", to: Letflow.Routers.Identity)`) -- there is no `/users`, `/admin/users`, `/admin/roles`, `/admin/groups`, or `/auth/tokens` forward anywhere in that pipeline (full forward list read directly, lines 141-194: /identity, /tenants, /tenant/settings, /instances, /definitions, /tasks, /promotions, /onboarding, /solution-packs, /audit, /dlq, /webhooks, /services, /admin/services, /entities, /exam-sessions, /public-read-handles, /help, /platform-migrations, /event-retention -- no bare /admin/users|roles|groups or /users or /auth/tokens mount exists or ever has). lib/letflow/routers/identity.ex's own routes (read in full) are all relative to that single /identity mount: `authz_get "/users"` -> real path `/api/v1/identity/users`; `authz_get "/roles"` -> real path `/api/v1/identity/roles`; `authz_post "/users"` -> `/api/v1/identity/users`; `authz_patch "/users/:id"` -> `/api/v1/identity/users/:id`; `authz_get "/users/:id"` -> `/api/v1/identity/users/:id`. web/src/api/identity.ts's usersApi and rolesApi objects hardcode paths under a different, nonexistent prefix -- there has never been a working route at any of those hardcoded paths.

REPRODUCTION (real, not restated): started the backend for real against this checkout's own docker containers (letflow-postgres-1 on host port 5462, letflow-keycloak-1 on host port 8093 -- both already running and healthy, confirmed via `docker ps`; no new containers started, no collision with sibling sessions' own wf03-iss0771-.../letflow-wf03-iss0768-... containers, which are on different names/projects). Ran `LETFLOW_DEV_DB_CONFIRMED=1 mix run --no-halt` (after sourcing this checkout's own .env for LETFLOW_SECRETS_MASTER_KEY/LETFLOW_KEYCLOAK_PORT) -- log confirms `Running Letflow.Router with Bandit 1.12.5 at 0.0.0.0:4000`. Obtained a real JWT via Keycloak's password grant (`POST http://localhost:8093/realms/bpm-default/protocol/openid-connect/token`, client_id=letflow-web, admin-user/admin-pass -- same mechanism web/tests/e2e/helpers.ts's getKeycloakToken uses), 1199-byte access_token confirmed non-empty. curl'd both the broken and real paths with that bearer token against the live backend:

  404   /api/v1/users
  404   /api/v1/admin/roles
  403   /api/v1/identity/users
  403   /api/v1/identity/roles
  404   /api/v1/admin/groups
  403   /api/v1/identity/groups
  404   /api/v1/auth/tokens
  403   /api/v1/identity/tokens

The 404-vs-403 split is itself the proof: 404 means Letflow.Router's own catch-all (no forward matched the path at all -- Plug never even reached AuthorizedRouter's policy check); 403 means the request WAS routed into Letflow.Routers.Identity and reached its authz_get/UsersManage|RolesManage policy check, which then denied this particular token (admin-user's Keycloak-realm role set is not provisioned with UsersManage/RolesManage in this dev realm -- a separate, unrelated authorization concern, not a routing defect). A 403 is only reachable once a route has actually matched, so it independently confirms /api/v1/identity/users and /api/v1/identity/roles are real, router-backed paths while /api/v1/users and /api/v1/admin/roles are not, exactly as ISS-0782 states. Backend process was stopped (taskkill on the erl.exe PID) after reproduction to leave the shared checkout as found; the already-running postgres/keycloak containers were left untouched since other sessions may depend on them.

CONFIRMED CORRECT ROUTES: `GET /api/v1/identity/users` (user listing) and `GET /api/v1/identity/roles` (role listing) -- both real, both matched by Letflow.Router before hitting authz, both distinct from the nonexistent /api/v1/users and /api/v1/admin/roles the SPA currently calls.

SCOPE -- what the Users admin screen actually calls (verified by grep across web/src/pages/admin/UsersPage.tsx and UserDetailPage.tsx, not the whole identity.ts file): UsersPage.tsx calls usersApi.list (GET), rolesApi.list (GET), usersApi.create (POST) via useAdminUsers.ts's useCreateAdminUser. UserDetailPage.tsx calls usersApi.get (GET, via useAdminUser), usersApi.update (PATCH, via useUpdateAdminUser AND useDeactivateAdminUser -- both route through the same usersApi.update), rolesApi.list (GET, via useAdminRoles), and groupsApi.list (GET, via useAdminGroups -- used to render a user's group memberships on the detail page). Cross-checked each hardcoded path in web/src/api/identity.ts against the router:

  usersApi.list    : GET  '/api/v1/users'              -> WRONG, real: GET  /api/v1/identity/users
  usersApi.get     : GET  '/api/v1/users/:id'           -> WRONG, real: GET  /api/v1/identity/users/:id
  usersApi.create  : POST '/api/v1/admin/users'         -> WRONG, real: POST /api/v1/identity/users
  usersApi.update  : PATCH '/api/v1/users/:id'          -> WRONG, real: PATCH /api/v1/identity/users/:id
  rolesApi.list    : GET  '/api/v1/admin/roles'         -> WRONG, real: GET  /api/v1/identity/roles

These five call sites are the complete, verified in-scope fix target: every one is actually reachable from the Users admin screen (UsersPage.tsx / UserDetailPage.tsx) and every one has a real, confirmed router-backed replacement path.

EXPLICITLY OUT OF SCOPE (do not fix as part of this issue -- noted so CODE-DESIGNER doesn't inadvertently scope-creep or, conversely, leave a call the Users screen depends on unfixed):
  - groupsApi.list (GET '/api/v1/admin/groups', also wrong, real path /api/v1/identity/groups) IS called by UserDetailPage.tsx (via useAdminGroups) and so is, strictly, reachable from the Users admin screen -- but it is also already the explicit subject of ISS-0765 (open, MAJOR, filed against groupsApi's entire broken-prefix set including .list). Flagging this overlap explicitly for CODE-DESIGNER: either (a) include this one shared call site in this fix since it is directly in-scope of 'the Users admin screen works', noting in the design that it also closes part of ISS-0765's scope, or (b) leave it to ISS-0765 and accept that UserDetailPage's group-membership section stays broken until that issue is worked -- CODE-DESIGNER's call, not ISSUE-FIXER's, but the acceptance criterion 'Users admin screen is functional' is not fully met by fixing only the five usersApi/rolesApi call sites above if groupsApi.list is left broken, since UserDetailPage would still throw loading group memberships.
  - usersApi.resetPassword (POST '/api/v1/users/:id/reset-password') and usersApi.delete (DELETE '/api/v1/users/:id') -- NOT called from any admin page (grepped web/src/pages and web/src/hooks; no caller found), AND no matching backend route exists at any prefix (lib/letflow/routers/identity.ex has no /users/:id/reset-password or DELETE /users/:id handler at all -- confirmed by reading the full route list, lines 158-225). Fixing identity.ts's path here would not make these functional; the backend endpoint itself does not exist. Out of scope -- a missing-backend-endpoint gap, not a frontend routing defect, and not blocking the Users screen since nothing calls them.
  - rolesApi.get/.create/.update/.delete/.grantPermission/.revokePermission, tokensApi.* -- none are called by UsersPage.tsx/UserDetailPage.tsx (confirmed by grep: rolesApi is used only via rolesApi.list across the whole web/src tree; tokensApi has zero callers outside TokensPage.tsx). Belong to other admin screens or are dead code; out of scope for this issue.

WHY EXISTING TESTS DIDN'T CATCH IT: grepped web/src for any test referencing usersApi/rolesApi/identity.ts/UsersPage -- the only test touching web/src/api/identity.ts at all is web/src/api/__tests__/identity.removeMembers.test.ts (ISS-0736's regression test), which covers exactly one groupsApi call and nothing in usersApi or rolesApi. No unit/component test exists for UsersPage.tsx or UserDetailPage.tsx that asserts the real fetch URL the way identity.removeMembers.test.ts does (spy on window.fetch, assert the exact path). web/tests/e2e/f5-admin-users.e2e.spec.ts DOES exist and drives a real browser against a real backend through these exact pages -- but its presence does not contradict this finding: it drives /admin/users through Playwright, meaning it WOULD have caught this had it been run against a live backend recently; UAT-RUNNER's own discovery of ISS-0782 in run WF02-REQ384-20260922 (per the issue's discovered_in_run) is the first time this surfaced, implying the e2e suite either wasn't being run against a real backend on a regular cadence, or a mocked/component-level substitute was relied on instead for day-to-day CI. Either way, the gap is the same one WF-03's own template calls out: mocked unit tests (identity.removeMembers.test.ts's pattern, correctly used for groupsApi.removeMembers) were never extended to usersApi/rolesApi, and the one real e2e test that could have caught this (f5-admin-users.e2e.spec.ts) evidently wasn't exercised against a live instance before this UAT run. TEST-DESIGNER should add a mocked fetch-URL assertion test for identity.ts's usersApi/rolesApi call sites mirroring identity.removeMembers.test.ts's exact convention (spy on window.fetch, assert exact path/method), per WF-03 Step 4's fail-then-pass requirement.
result.next_action: Route to CODE-DESIGNER for fix design
